# 🛰️ First Satellite vs. Latest Satellite (2026)

---

## 🚀 SPUTNIK 1 — The World's First Satellite (1957)

Sputnik 1 was the first artificial Earth satellite, launched into an elliptical low Earth orbit by the Soviet Union on **4 October 1957**.

- **Size & Weight:** Only about the size of a beach ball — 22.8 inches (58 cm) in diameter — and weighing 183.9 pounds (83.6 kg), it orbited the Earth in around **98 minutes**.

- **Design:** It was an extremely simple satellite — a metal sphere with four long antennas protruding from it. It contained a thermometer, a fan, a radio transmitter, batteries, and little else.

- **Purpose:** The only cargo onboard Sputnik was a low-power radio transmitter, which broadcast a beeping noise at regular intervals — a signal that could be heard by radio listeners around the world.

- **Orbit:** Sputnik 1's orbit was elliptical — approximately 230 km from Earth at its closest point (perigee) and 940 km away at its furthest point (apogee).

- **Lifespan:** The satellite transmitters operated for **three weeks**, until the on-board chemical batteries failed. The orbit of the then-inactive satellite decayed 92 days after launch, on January 4, 1958, after completing about **1,400 orbits** of the Earth over a cumulative distance of 70 million kilometers.

- **Speed:** It orbited Earth at 29,000 kilometers per hour (18,000 miles per hour).

- **Historical Impact:** The satellite's success was unanticipated by the United States, which precipitated the American Sputnik crisis and triggered the start of the **Space Race**.

---

## 🛰️ VIASAT-3 F3 — One of the Latest Satellites (2026)

SpaceX launched the final ViaSat-3 satellite on **April 29, 2026**, to complete Viasat's trio of high-capacity Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellites, lifting off on a **Falcon Heavy** from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida.

- **Platform:** Built on Boeing's high-power **702MP+ platform** and integrated at Boeing's El Segundo facility in California.

- **Purpose:** The satellite is intended to provide broadband connectivity with speeds of **100+ megabits per second** to homes, businesses, enterprise internet users, commercial and government aircraft, defense markets, and maritime enterprises.

- **Capacity:** Designed to deliver over **1 Terabit per second (Tbps)** of throughput capacity, the satellite leverages innovative payload design and advanced beam-forming technology to optimize and steer immense capacity in real time.

- **Coverage:** The ViaSat-3 satellites are each designed to provide regional coverage, with ViaSat-3 F3 covering the **Asia-Pacific (APAC) region**.

- **Orbit Type:** Launching on a Falcon Heavy rocket reduces time to orbit by delivering the satellite to a more favorable transfer orbit, where the satellite's **electric propulsion** takes over to place ViaSat-3 F3 in **geostationary orbit**. It will spend several months traveling to its final orbital slot.

- **Flexibility:** The VS-3 constellation is designed to rapidly shift capacity throughout its coverage area to deliver bandwidth where and when it's needed most, meeting the increasing demand of commercial mobility and defense customers.
